name: Ninam
catalog_quote: Utterances are divided into stress groups or feet; stress will occur on the final syllable of a foot, unless that foot occurs before a pause, then stress will be on the penultimate of the foot. (Hyman 1977:42)

audit.recode_to: fixed penultimate, dominant (penultimate stress; secondary stress two vowels to the left), citing Migliazza 1972:161-162 (A.P.1/A.P.2) as deciding source and M&G 1961:35,37 as the phrase-level surface description; add caution: word-final unstressed vowels elide/devoice at non-pause word boundaries (1972:166-167), so phrase-medial words surface with final stress — the basis of StressTyp2/WALS 'ultimate'. Domain stays word and phrase together/phrase-sensitive; keep out of the strict set. If the catalog prefers not to reclassify on one author's reanalysis, minimum action is re-read-with-listed-source (Migliazza 1972, held) and cite both.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding sentences are verbatim in the 1961 scan we hold at p.35 and p.37 (page image and text layer read). (2) The classification 'fixed-dominant, final' is StressTyp2's (and WALS's) reading of Migliazza & Grimes 1961, an 11-page taxonomic phonology whose stress statement is about feet inside pause groups; the clause that governs isolation/citation forms (pause-group-final foot) is penultimate, and only phrase-medial feet are final. The same fieldworker's 1972 Indiana dissertation on the same variety but not cited in the catalog record) gives an explicit word-domain rule — penultimate primary stress, secondary two vowels before it — marks phrase-medial words penult too (p.162), and derives phrase-medial surface-final stress from deletion/devoicing of the post-tonic final vowel at non-pause wor

sources.quote: p. 35: "Every foot also has one loud stress. This occurs on the penault [sic] or ultima of the foot — on the penult of a foot that is at the end of a pause group, on the ultima of all other feet. Accordingly, the minimum foot that can occur at the end of a pause group is a two-syllable one, whereas the minimum foot that can occur elsewhere is a one-syllable one." p. 37: "Paroxytonic feet occur only at the end of pause groups; all other feet are oxytonic."

sources.quote: p.161: 'Primary stress is assigned to the penultimate vowel of underlying phonological words.' p.162 A.P.1: 'primary stress is assigned on the penultimate vowel of a word and to the last vowel if the word is monosyllabic. The rule A.P.1 as specified would not assign stress with just a morpheme boundary, but would assign it with word and pause boundary.' A.P.2: 'secondary stress is placed on the second vowel preceding the primary stressed vowel.' Examples with phrase-medial words penult-stressed: % maamá+kə # rothóte # čài+óma % 'the stones were really hard'; % šáma # kìteénə % 'same as a tapir
